title: Zetwerk Lists at 5% Premium, Ends Debut 8% Below Issue Price as Early Backers Book 38x
excerpt: Shares opened at Rs 159 against a Rs 151 issue price but closed at Rs 138.30 in Peak XV Partners' 30th portfolio listing, a Rs 5,012 crore IPO subscribed 3.1 times.
body:
• Zetwerk Manufacturing Businesses listed at Rs 159 on the BSE and NSE on October 23 — a premium of about 5.5% over its Rs 151 issue price — but closed its debut at Rs 138.30, down 8.4% from the issue price.
  • The Rs 5,012 crore IPO (fresh issue Rs 2,830 crore, offer for sale Rs 2,182 crore) was subscribed 3.1 times, led by institutions; anchor investors put in Rs 2,251.2 crore.
  • It was Peak XV Partners' 30th portfolio listing; Kae Capital Fund II and Kalysta Capital Fund II booked gross returns of about 38.3x on shares acquired at a weighted average Rs 3.94.
  • At the closing price, Zetwerk's market capitalisation stood at Rs 23,431.54 crore (about $2.4 billion), below the $2.7 billion valuation at the top of its price band.

Zetwerk Manufacturing Businesses, the Bengaluru-based B2B manufacturing platform, endured a weak first day on the public markets on Friday: the shares listed at about a 5.5% premium and then slid all session to close 8.4% below the issue price, even as the listing delivered venture-scale returns to its earliest backers.

The stock listed at Rs 159 on both exchanges — Rs 159.25 on the NSE, a 5.46% premium to the Rs 151 issue price — and reached intraday highs of Rs 160.50-161 before selling set in, according to Moneycontrol. It closed at Rs 138.30 on the BSE and Rs 138.25 on the NSE, down 8.4% from the issue price and about 13% from the listing price, according to the Inc42 update carried by MSN. At that close, market capitalisation was Rs 23,431.54 crore, about $2.4 billion.

The issue

The Rs 5,012.33 crore IPO — a fresh issue of Rs 2,830 crore plus an offer for sale of Rs 2,182 crore (144.5 million shares) — was priced in a Rs 143-151 band that valued the company at Rs 25,583 crore ($2.7 billion) at the top end. The issue, open October 15-19, was subscribed 3.1 times overall, led by institutional demand while the retail portion was undersubscribed; anchor investors contributed Rs 2,251.2 crore for 149.1 million shares. Proceeds from the fresh issue are earmarked for debt repayment and acquisitions.

A payday for early backers

The listing was Peak XV Partners' 30th portfolio listing. Kae Capital, Accel, Peak XV and Lightspeed together sold 76.3 million shares — more than half the offer for sale — with total realisations by selling investors put at about Rs 1,215 crore at the issue price by Moneycontrol. The standout multiples belong to the earliest money: Kae Capital Fund II and Kalysta Capital Fund II recorded gross returns of about 38.3x on shares acquired at a weighted average of Rs 3.94, with Kae set to realise about Rs 190 crore and Kalysta about Rs 63 crore from their sales.

What to watch

For diaspora investors following Indian listings, Zetwerk is a test of appetite for B2B industrial platforms: institutional demand carried the issue, retail stayed cautious, and the debut tape punished the valuation anyway. Whether the stock reclaims its Rs 151 issue price will depend on order-book conversion and the debt-repayment plan, not on first-day sentiment.
nri_angle: Zetwerk's debut is a benchmark Indian industrial-tech listing for diaspora investors tracking India exposure through GIFT City and NRI investment routes.
